answer: An exit-burn registry makes shedding bad history costly. Each identity stakes 120 credits; exit burns 60, and re-entry waits ten epochs at zero weight. The ivory ledger holds conduct until exit, so no flagged operator returns clean for free. The k-th washed identity costs 120 credits plus a 60-credit burn, so 1,000 washes burn 60,000 credits, halving capital each wash, never reused. An echo check matches new keys against the burned registry. A mirror rule rejects copies of burned profiles, blocking sale-based dodging. An honest agent stakes 120 once and keeps full weight.
